answer: Cap influence by network independence: each identity must prove it runs on a distinct endpoint, triangulated by latency probes from peers, and each subnet earns only a small slice of total weight. A farm of ten thousand clones behind one datacenter is an orchard planted in a single pot — no matter how many branches it grows, the pot caps its share. Buying diversity costs money per endpoint, and a violet flag rises when many identities answer probes from the same lagoon of addresses. Limits: proxy markets sell diversity, and honest users behind shared campus networks get throttled too.
